$schema_note: Live points that hs_game_sdk.movement_speed_model is checked against (tests/test_movement_speed_model.py, MeasuredTests); the mechanism is docs/models/movement-speed-spec.md. ForgePact#166 phase 2, Mod live procedure 1, 2026-10-19, research build of ForgePact 109c908 (SHA-256 a2f64cf3889a4333e03c4fb0667045799b5fcb05f91e535c9fc171ff154ea493), save slot 14, character Sorak (White Mage), in Town_01_rm, every shipped mod off. Each sweep window held D down from the town waypoint and ran `mark1probe stat 64 <m> 240` (the dispatcher's id-64 answer multiplied by m on every local call for 240 frames) beside `mark1probe pos 240` (the window's modal step per frame and its mean frame time, ms). A ratio is the window's modal step over the control's 2.989 px, and is valid only when the window's ms is within 10% of the control's 6.945 (RDM section 19.10). MS9 is phase 1's Live 2 (2026-10-13), the same character and save at 13.4 ms a frame. Captures are cited by file name (forgepact-166-mark1-set-mod-live-1.md, forgepact-166-mark1-set-live-2.md) and stay with the hub's workorder files; the argument is ForgePact docs/mark1-set-research.md section Mod live 1 results. A status is measured, or not established for a value no window printed.

measurements.what: Two unlevered D walks from the town waypoint: modal step 2.989 px both, at 6.94 and 6.95 ms a frame.
During a walk the dispatcher answered id 64 once a frame, 151 on all 60 frames, every call outside the probe's twenty rows, and StatMovementSpeed was never called outside the dispatcher.
measurements.model: the reference answer every sweep ratio is taken against

measurements.what: Answer x1.5 on all 240 dispatcher calls of the window.
Answer x0.75 on all 240 dispatcher calls of the window.
Answer x0.5 on all 240 dispatcher calls of the window: 0.785, not 0.5.
Answer x0.25 on all 240 dispatcher calls of the window.
Answer x0 (an answer of 0) on all 240 dispatcher calls of the window: the walk still moves, at 0.570.
Answer x-0.5 (an answer of -75.5) on all 240 dispatcher calls of the window: a negative answer slows the walk further and it still moves forward.
The multiplier interpolated between the -0.5 and 0 windows, -0.162 (an answer of about -24.5, that is (151 - 200) / 2), gave a ratio of 0.500.

Phase 1's Live 2 halved the dispatcher's id-64 answer for 240 frames at 13.4 ms a frame: the modal step went from 5.979 px to 4.693 px, 0.785. The answer itself was not printed in that session; the same character and save answered 151 in Mod live 1, which the replay assumes.

The same unlevered walk had a modal step of 5.979 px at 13.4 ms a frame (phase 1) and 2.989 px at 6.94 ms (Mod live 1): a step ratio of 0.500 at a frame-time ratio of 0.518; a step proportional to frame time would be about 3.10 px. The cause (the frame clock, a target-rate setting or a per-frame constant) is not established, so the model takes each window's scale as a parameter.
measurements.model: step_per_point_from(step, 151) for each window; not a constant of the model
